allowed_claims: Plausible Analytics is built to enable customers to comply with GDPR, CCPA and other privacy regulations that impact their business.
Plausible encrypts data in transit using TLS 1.2 or newer, with TLS 1.3 preferred.
Plausible uses hashing techniques so visitor data cannot be reversed or used to identify individuals, with rotating salts adding extra protection.
Plausible generates a daily changing identifier from the visitor's IP address and User-Agent, anonymized by running them through a hash function with a rotating salt.
Plausible rotates and deletes the hashing salt every 24 hours.
Plausible never stores the raw IP address and User-Agent in logs, databases or anywhere on disk.
All visitor data is kept encrypted in Germany on servers owned by Hetzner, a German company.
Customers control how their data is shared: they can invite users, assign permissions, create shared links, configure email reports, or make dashboards public.
Backups are encrypted with AES-256, stored in the EU, retained for 30 days, and used only for recovery purposes.
If a breach affects customer data, Plausible notifies the customer without undue delay and no later than 48 hours after becoming aware of it.
Plausible uses a limited number of subprocessors where necessary, carefully selected and bound by data protection agreements.
Plausible aims for continuous availability but does not guarantee uninterrupted service; current and historical uptime is published on its status page.
Plausible's code is open source and publicly available, allowing independent verification of its security and privacy practices.
Plausible doesn't collect or store personal data about website visitors that can be used to identify individuals.
Plausible does not store visitor data outside the EU.
The official Data Studio connector lets users build custom dashboards, branded client reports, and views that blend Plausible data with other sources like ad spend or CRM data.
Plausible lets you import your Google Analytics history so the dashboard starts with your full data record.
Plausible requires no cookies, no personal data collection, and no consent banners.
Plausible's compliance documentation covers GDPR, CCPA and data processing.
Plausible's user journeys feature lets users explore the paths visitors take on a site.
Plausible's Stats API allows programmatic querying of analytics data.

The Business plan is needed for funnels, user journeys, revenue tracking, custom properties, Stats API or Data Studio, which can build custom dashboards and blend Plausible data with other sources like ad spend or CRM data.
Enterprise's scheduled raw event data exports deliver event- and session-level data daily to the customer's S3-compatible object storage.
Plausible's subscription tier is based on the total number of pageviews and custom events across all sites in a team.
Plausible measures drop-off across a fixed sequence of steps and lets users explore the paths visitors actually take.
Plausible does not use cookies, persistent identifiers, or cross-site/cross-device tracking, and does not use site data for any other purposes.
All visitor data is exclusively processed on servers owned and operated by European companies and never leaves the EU.
Plausible's Business plan includes a Stats API with a limit of 600 requests per hour.

assets.content:
Subject: Control access to performance data
Preview text: Test permissions, shared links, email reports and public dashboards in one reporting workflow.

Hi there,

Sharing performance data does not have to mean giving every stakeholder the same dashboard access. Plausible lets teams invite users and assign permissions, then create shared links, configure email reports or make a dashboard public.

Plausible Analytics is hosted web analytics software with several ways to control how website data is shared. Those options can support distinct routes for internal access and published performance data.

A 30-day trial provides a practical way to inspect these controls in the product. Use a representative reporting workflow to see which permissions colleagues need, what a shared link exposes and whether an email report or public dashboard suits the intended audience.

The result is a concrete basis for deciding whether Plausible fits the team’s access and publication approach.

Start a 30-day free trial → https://plausible.io/register

- the Plausible Analytics team

brief.orientation: For an EU or UK public sector web team, Plausible is a hosted web analytics product whose documentation states it uses no cookies and collects no personal data about visitors, and that visitor data is processed only on EU servers — the material an Information Governance or DPIA review of an analytics tool has to assess.

emails.selection_reason: The no-cookie, no-identifiable-personal-data design directly addresses the privacy and governance questions this audience must assess. A trial lets the team determine whether the resulting analytics are useful enough for its own reporting requirements.
emails.job: Earn a 30-day product evaluation against the team's analytics, Information Governance and DPIA requirements.
emails.single_idea: Plausible is worth evaluating when a government digital team needs useful web analytics without cookies or identifiable visitor data, backed by a documented anonymisation mechanism and EU-only processing.
emails.mechanism: Plausible uses no cookies. allowed_claims: Plausible Analytics is built to enable customers to comply with GDPR, CCPA and other privacy regulations that impact their business.
Plausible encrypts data in transit using TLS 1.2 or newer, with TLS 1.3 preferred.
Plausible uses hashing techniques so visitor data cannot be reversed or used to identify individuals, with rotating salts adding extra protection.
Plausible generates a daily changing identifier from the visitor's IP address and User-Agent, anonymized by running them through a hash function with a rotating salt.
Plausible rotates and deletes the hashing salt every 24 hours.
Plausible never stores the raw IP address and User-Agent in logs, databases or anywhere on disk.
All visitor data is kept encrypted in Germany on servers owned by Hetzner, a German company.
Customers control how their data is shared: they can invite users, assign permissions, create shared links, configure email reports, or make dashboards public.
Backups are encrypted with AES-256, stored in the EU, retained for 30 days, and used only for recovery purposes.
If a breach affects customer data, Plausible notifies the customer without undue delay and no later than 48 hours after becoming aware of it.
Plausible uses a limited number of subprocessors where necessary, carefully selected and bound by data protection agreements.
Plausible aims for continuous availability but does not guarantee uninterrupted service; current and historical uptime is published on its status page.
Plausible's code is open source and publicly available, allowing independent verification of its security and privacy practices.
Plausible doesn't collect or store personal data about website visitors that can be used to identify individuals.
Plausible does not store visitor data outside the EU.
The official Data Studio connector lets users build custom dashboards, branded client reports, and views that blend Plausible data with other sources like ad spend or CRM data.
Plausible lets you import your Google Analytics history so the dashboard starts with your full data record.
Plausible requires no cookies, no personal data collection, and no consent banners.
Plausible's compliance documentation covers GDPR, CCPA and data processing.
Plausible's user journeys feature lets users explore the paths visitors take on a site.
Plausible's Stats API allows programmatic querying of analytics data.

The Business plan is needed for funnels, user journeys, revenue tracking, custom properties, Stats API or Data Studio, which can build custom dashboards and blend Plausible data with other sources like ad spend or CRM data.
Enterprise's scheduled raw event data exports deliver event- and session-level data daily to the customer's S3-compatible object storage.
Plausible's subscription tier is based on the total number of pageviews and custom events across all sites in a team.
Plausible measures drop-off across a fixed sequence of steps and lets users explore the paths visitors actually take.
Plausible does not use cookies, persistent identifiers, or cross-site/cross-device tracking, and does not use site data for any other purposes.
All visitor data is exclusively processed on servers owned and operated by European companies and never leaves the EU.
Plausible's Business plan includes a Stats API with a limit of 600 requests per hour.
